title: Dear Alice (Chobani advertisement)
lede: A one-minute 2D animated advertisement in which a grandmother’s letter to her granddaughter narrates a future of farms under solar panels and green cities.
summary: Hand-drawn animated ad of a solarpunk farming future, scored by Joe Hisaishi. The Line for Chobani, 2021.

creator.name: The Line, directed by Bjørn-Erik Aschim

evidence.note: Based on the studio’s project page and the Looper article (2023). The film was not watched and no still was inspected.

styles.note: The style record names this advertisement as the model for solarpunk motion, and Looper calls it a one-minute summary of the genre.

context: The Line, a London animation studio, lists “Dear Alice” for client Chobani: director Bjørn-Erik Aschim, June 2021, length 1:00, music by Joe Hisaishi, art director Antoine Perez, producer Samia Ahmed, animation lead Bishoy Gendi. The studio describes it as “a love letter from a grandmother to a granddaughter and an optimistic vision of the future of farming”. [The Line](https://thelinestudio.com/work/chobani).

Looper says the opening images show sustainable farming combined with modern technology, “such as a cow grazing while solar panels are overhead”, and that the view then pulls out to a city whose buildings incorporate greenery. It says the ad “distills the genre into one minute”. [Looper, 15 November 2023](https://www.looper.com/1446464/what-is-solarpunk-dear-alice-ad-explained/).

Joe Hisaishi is known for his scores for Studio Ghibli films, and press coverage compared the ad’s look with Ghibli. [Nerdist](https://nerdist.com/article/dear-alice-solarpunk-anime-short-studio-ghibli-composer/).
interpretation: The ad brought the solarpunk look to a mass audience and fixed its motion grammar: slow pans across fields, wind in grass and leaves, and soft daylight.
It is also a brand film for a food company, so it shows the greenwashing risk that the style’s rules warn about.
borrow: Use slow camera moves and natural motion (wind, light, grazing animals) in place of fast cuts.
